title: Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids: The Whole Chapter in One Minute
subject: Chemistry
objective: The chapter in one place: the polar, planar C=O group; how aldehydes and ketones are made; nucleophilic addition; aldol and Cannizzaro; Tollens' and Fehling's tests; and why carboxylic acids are acidic.

fill.q: In C=O, the oxygen carries a partial ____ charge.
Aldehydes without an α-hydrogen give the ____ reaction.
Aldehydes give a silver mirror with ____ reagent.

tf.q: The typical reaction of aldehydes and ketones is nucleophilic addition.
tf.explain: The nucleophile attacks the δ⁺ carbonyl carbon.

tf.q: Ketones give a red precipitate with Fehling's solution.
tf.explain: Ketones generally do not reduce Fehling's solution.

tf.q: Electron-withdrawing groups increase the acidity of carboxylic acids.

ar.a: Aldehydes and ketones undergo nucleophilic addition.
Carboxylic acids are more acidic than alcohols.
ar.r: The carboxylate ion is stabilised by resonance.

mcq.explain: O₃, then Zn/H₂O, cleaves the C=C.

mcq.q: Which compound gives the aldol reaction?
HCN adds to a ketone to give:
mcq.explain: The CN⁻ attacks the carbonyl carbon.

num.q: What is the approximate bond angle around the carbonyl carbon, in degrees?

short.q: Give a chemical test to distinguish ethanal from propanone.
short.solution: Ethanal gives a silver mirror with Tollens' reagent (and a red-brown precipitate with Fehling's solution); propanone does not.
